title: CrashLoopBackOff in checkout-service
intro: You're on call. PagerDuty says checkout-service is unstable in prod.

steps.fake_output:
NAME                               READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
checkout-service-7f9d8b6c5-x2z9k   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   5          4m
steps.hint: You need to see what's actually running first.

steps.fake_output:
Error: connection refused to db-service:5432
FATAL: could not connect to database, exiting
steps.hint: Logs will show the failure reason. If the current container has no logs yet, try --previous.

steps.prompt: Check if the database service it depends on even exists.
steps.fake_output:
NAME         TYPE        CLUSTER-IP    PORT(S)
db-service   ClusterIP   None          5432/TCP
steps.hint: The app is failing to reach 'db-service' — does that service exist and look healthy?

steps.prompt: The service exists but CLUSTER-IP is 'None' — check the endpoints to see if it actually has any pods behind it.
steps.hint: No endpoints means the service's label selector isn't matching any running pods.

steps.prompt: Check the actual database pod status.
steps.fake_output:
NAME       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
db-0       0/1     Pending   0          2h
steps.hint: Look for pods matching the database's label.

steps.prompt: The db pod is stuck Pending. Find out why.
steps.fake_output:
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2h  0/3 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient memory.
steps.hint: describe shows scheduling events at the bottom.

resolution: The database pod couldn't be scheduled due to insufficient memory on all nodes, so it never started, which meant db-service had no endpoints, which meant checkout-service couldn't connect and kept crash-looping. The real fix would be freeing up node memory (scaling the cluster, reducing other pods' requests, or increasing node size), not restarting checkout-service — that pod was innocent.
